text_post: RE: how much are rape and assault of women connected to misogyny? I'd suggest that, since the definition of "rape" has been adjusted over and over to strictly forbid it as being possible for a woman to rape a man, that rape, at least in part, can be contributed to misandry. Now, as for the rape and assault of women in particular? Mmm... the definitions have gotten really ridiculously vague, to the point that most of these cases, if you can consider them such anymore, have nothing to do with it even being a woman in the first place. However... yeah, there are cases where there really are guys who are fucking pricks out there. There are women that are total assholes as well. Humans suck, and that's just kind of true in general, so there will always be examples of both ends of that spectrum. What's been found, however, is that abuse in the form of violence, at least, comes primarily from growing up with being abused or told that it's alright to abuse someone. This has been shown to be primarily taught by the mother, rather than the father, so both misandry and misogyny tend to come from the same source: a cruel mother figure who takes it out on males. If you're a male, you'll probably assume it's alright to be abusive and start to hate women in general; if you're female, you'll probably go with being a second generation man-hater. Even so... are rape and assault primarily because of misogyny? In the most extreme cases, almost guaranteed. The worst of the worst our species has to offer will probably be misogynists or misandronists, or racist, or some other effect. These are the ones that make the headlines. The regular cases however? Probably a different story, for the most part. Abusive relationships tend to be a two-way affair where both parties hate each other, or if it's one sided, then it's about a 2:1 ratio of females beating the shit out of males, rather than the other way around. As such, I'm going to suggest that only about the estimated 14% of one-way abusive relationships that are male-against-female will be misogynistic in nature at best. Considering there may be other reasons for some of these, the chances are closer to 10-12% probably. This is for domestic violence against women, however. In terms of things like rape? Harder to say. Are we using definitions like "asking for sex and getting a hesitant yes, then being told afterward that the consent was removed post-event because she decided she was pressured into it"? If so, then... no. If it's more like "let's drug her and fuck her brains out"? Then yes. I think the more important question to be asking, here, is "what can women realistically change about the world to prevent rape and abuse from happening in the first place?". The answer to that, largely involves actually USING that goddamned empowerment we keep saying we have. "I feel so empowered!" Really. Do you now. Did you use that empowerment to change your choices, alter your environment, or otherwise take responsibility for your actions? Did you actually use that POWER, because that's what empowerment means, to realize you have a hand in your own destiny? GirlWritesWhat said in one case that she thought it was a little silly that women at her workplace would request someone walk them to their cars after work, because of how scary that 40 meter trip must be. To be blunt though, she should be praising them; they're taking their own lives into their own hands; they're being responsible for their actions, and realizing that they can actually do stuff to alter the outcome of their lives. If you walk down the middle of the bronx at 3am in the nude, you'd damned well better expect to be either killed, raped, attacked, or some combination of those things, male or female. The thing is, males have realized they have the power to go "yeah, that's fucking retarded, why would I do that?", while women have been told they're useless and incapable of doing anything to change fate, and it's all men's fault so don't victim blame when they willingly stick their hand in a fucking blender, then get pissy when someone turns it on. Psst, if you didn't stick your hand in the blender in the first place, they couldn't turn your hand into hamburger. Just saying. The greatest misogyny here of all, is not the asshole rapists themselves, but the fact that feminists have managed to give women a "warm fuzzy feeling of empowerment", despite not actually fucking empowering them, but instead teaching them they're incapable of doing anything, and have zero power at all. I'm transgendered; this doesn't mean much normally, but when it comes to getting raped for walking down the street, I'm several orders of magnitude above cisgendered women for getting raped. I have the power to say that I'll take the long way home because it's a ton safer, and that I can choose my own fate, at least in part. I might still get raped anyway some day, but that will be out of my hands if and when it happens. For now, I can severely reduce the chances by telling feminism to stop telling me I'm incapable of preventing anything, and actually actively prevent it. The biggest misogynist in all of this is feminism; it exists in virtually every rape and violent case there is out there, and restricts people from using their own common sense to protect themselves.
